content2.content: When your Flutter application needs to store data locally on the device, you have several options, from simple key-value stores like shared_preferences to relational databases like sqflite. For many apps, a powerful middle ground is needed: a solution that is faster and more powerful than key-value stores but easier to use than raw SQL.

content3.content: Enter ObjectBox, a super-fast, ACID-compliant NoSQL database designed for mobile and IoT devices. It provides a simple, object-oriented API, eliminating the need to write complex SQL queries.

content4.content: What is ObjectBox and Why Use It?

content5.content: ObjectBox is an embedded object database. This means you work directly with your Dart objects, and ObjectBox handles storing and retrieving them efficiently.

content7.content:
Blazing Fast: It's built for performance and is significantly faster than SQLite-based solutions for most common operations.
Easy to Use: You interact with your data using a simple, object-oriented API. No need to write SQL queries.

NoSQL Structure: It's a document-oriented database, which often maps more naturally to object-oriented languages like Dart
Compile-Time Safety: It uses code generation to create type-safe code, which helps catch errors before you run your app.
Built-in Relations: Easily define one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationships between your data objects.
Scalable: It's suitable for apps with large amounts of data and complex query needs.

content9.content: Setting Up ObjectBox in Your Flutter Project

content10.content: Setting up ObjectBox involves adding dependencies and using Flutter's build system to generate necessary code.

content12.content: Add the following packages to your pubspec.yaml file:

content13.content:
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  objectbox: ^2.0.0 # Use the latest version
  objectbox_flutter_libs: ^2.0.0 # Use the latest version

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  build_runner: ^2.0.0 # Use the latest version
  objectbox_generator: ^2.0.0 # Use the latest version

content14.content: Run flutter pub get to install the packages.

content16.content: An "Entity" is a Dart class that represents the data you want to store. You annotate a regular Dart class with @Entity to tell ObjectBox to create a "Box" for it (a Box is like a table in a relational database).

content17.content: Let's create a simple Task model.

content20.content:
@Entity(): Marks the class as a persistable ObjectBox entity.
@Id(): Marks an int property as the unique ID for each object. ObjectBox will automatically assign an ID when a new object is saved if id is 0.

content22.content: ObjectBox uses the build_runner package to generate a file named objectbox-model.json and a objectbox.g.dart file. This generated code contains all the necessary bindings to make your entities work with the database.

content33.content: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete. With your objectbox instance available, these operations are straightforward.

content35.content: To save a new object, you create an instance of your entity class and use box.put().

content38.content: To read an object, you can get it by its ID or get all objects in a box.

content41.content: For more complex reads, use the QueryBuilder.

content43.content: Note: Task_ is part of the code generated by build_runner and gives you type-safe access to your entity's properties for building queries.

content45.content: Updating an object is the same as creating one. If you put() an object that already has a non-zero id, ObjectBox will find the existing object and update its properties.

content48.content: To remove an object, you use box.remove() with the object's ID.

content51.content: ObjectBox provides a robust, developer-friendly, and incredibly fast solution for local data persistence in Flutter. Its simple object-oriented API lets you focus on your app's logic instead of writing complex database code. By handling entities, relationships, and queries in a type-safe manner, it helps you build scalable and maintainable applications that can efficiently manage local data. For any app that needs more than a simple key-value store, ObjectBox is a top-tier choice.
